# Demo 1: compromised bank A3 floods status checks

**Threat.** A3 is a valid switch client but sends status inquiries far above its share (here 150/s for 8 s) on the route that A1/A2 legitimately use (B).

**Trigger.** Track B's own A3 flooding generator (`run_flood`) against the in-process switch, while the integrated AORTS loop keeps running (telemetry -> controller -> execution gate -> checks).

| measured in this run (seed 101) | defences OFF | defences ON |
|---|---|---|
| legitimate (A1/A2) check success during attack | 0.8913 | 1.0 |
| legitimate check p95 latency during (ms) | 551.16 | 61.29 |
| A3 checks accepted / rejected (429) | 1050 / 0 | 99 / 1101 |
| A3 rejections: RATE_LIMITED / CREDIT_EXHAUSTED | 0 / 0 | 1101.0 / 0 |
| detection / containment (s) | None / None | 0.142 / 1.0 |
| route B payments closed per s during | 3.0 | 3.0 |
| payment p95 on B during (ms) | 353.77 | 168.21 |
| controller budget on A1-B before / during | 0.0 / 0.0 | 1.0 / 1.0 |
| controller recovery after attack (s) | None | 0.03 |
| ledger integrity / duplicate checks / second debits | True / 0 / 0 | True / 0 / 0 |

**Detection and enforcement.** Switch admission (per-bank token bucket, route and global limits, Tier-2 credits) rejects A3 before the worker pool; the controller sees the congestion only through the remitter's own telemetry and lowers or holds its budget; Track B's execution gate admits only what the decision and quotas allow.

Timelines (from the recorded ticks): `flood_undefended-timeline.svg`, `flood_defended-timeline.svg`.
